page_title: How To Deploy a Telegram Bot

summary.title: How To Deploy a Telegram Bot
summary.one_liner: You learn how to deploy a Python Django-based Telegram bot on a Digital Ocean Ubuntu VPS using nginx, gunicorn, supervisord, Let's Encrypt SSL and a Telegram webhook.
takeaways: Set up a sudo user, install Python via pyenv and clone the bot repo on an Ubuntu VPS.
Run a Django/WSGI app with gunicorn behind an nginx reverse proxy that uses a Let's Encrypt SSL certificate.
Use supervisord to keep gunicorn running and an upstart script to restart supervisord after reboot.
Register the Telegram webhook with setWebhook pointing at the public HTTPS domain.
summary.summary: The author walks through deploying a Django Telegram bot (the second part of a series) to a $5/month Digital Ocean droplet running Ubuntu 14.04. Steps cover server setup, installing Python 2.7.13 with pyenv, configuring environment variables with django-environ, and obtaining a Let's Encrypt certificate. The guide then configures nginx as a proxy to gunicorn on localhost:8001, manages gunicorn with supervisord, and adds an upstart script for restart on boot. It ends with a short script that sets the Telegram webhook. The method is noted to apply to any Python WSGI app such as Flask or Pyramid.
